24
::右集錄楚詞七家，帝王二十七家，太子諸王二十一家，七國趙、楚各一家，前漢二十家，後漢五十家，魏四十六家，蜀二家，吳十四家，西晉一百一十九家，東晉一百四十四家，宋六十家，南齊十二家，梁五十九家，陳十四家，後魏十家，北齊四家，週五家，隋十八家，唐一百一十二家，沙門七家，婦人七家； 總集一百二十四家。 凡八百九十二部，一萬二千二十八卷。 【結】三代之書，經秦燔煬殆盡。 漢武帝、河間王始重儒術，于灰燼之餘，拓纂亡散，篇卷僅而復存。 劉更生石渠典校之書，卷軸無幾。 逮歆之《七略》，在《漢藝文志》者，裁三萬三千九百卷。 後漢蘭台、石室、東觀、南宮諸儒撰集，部帙漸增。 董卓遷都，載舟西上，因罹寇盜，沉之於河，存者數船而已。 及魏武父子，采掇遺亡，至晉總括群書，裁二萬七千九百四十五卷。 及永嘉之亂，洛都覆沒，靡有孑遺。 江表所存官書，凡三千一十四卷。 至宋謝靈運造《四部書目錄》，凡四千五百八十二卷。 其後王儉復造書目，凡五千七十四卷。
Collected-works register listed above: Songs of Chu, 7 titles; emperors, 27 titles; crown princes and princes, 21 titles; the Seven States — Zhao and Chu, 1 title each; Former Han, 20 titles; Later Han, 50 titles; Wei, 46 titles; Shu, 2 titles; Wu, 14 titles; Western Jin, 119 titles; Eastern Jin, 144 titles; Song, 60 titles; Southern Qi, 12 titles; Liang, 59 titles; Chen, 14 titles; Later Wei, 10 titles; Northern Qi, 4 titles; Northern Zhou, 5 titles; Sui, 18 titles; Tang, 112 titles; monks, 7 titles; women, 7 titles; General anthologies: 124 titles. 892 titles in all, 12,028 scrolls. 【Conclusion】The books of the Three Dynasties were nearly all destroyed in Qin's burning. Emperor Wu of Han and the King of Hejian first revived Confucian learning; from the ashes they gathered what had been lost and scattered, and only a few chapters and scrolls survived. The books Liu Gengsheng collated at the Stone Canal Pavilion amounted to only a few scrolls. By the time of Liu Xin's Seven Summaries, as recorded in the Han Bibliographic Treatise, there were only 33,900 scrolls. In Later Han, scholar-officials at the Orchid Pavilion, Stone Chamber, Eastern View, and Southern Palace compiled and collected, and the number of titles and bundles gradually increased. When Dong Zhuo moved the capital, the books were loaded onto boats and sent west; bandits struck, and they were sunk in the river — only a few boatloads survived. When Cao Cao and his son gathered what had been lost, down to Jin's comprehensive compilation of all books, there were only 27,945 scrolls. When the Yongjia turmoil came, the capital at Luoyang was overrun, and scarcely a survivor remained. Official books preserved south of the Yangtze numbered 3,014 scrolls in all. By the time Xie Lingyun of Song compiled the Bibliographic Catalogue in Four Sections, there were 4,582 scrolls in all. Afterward Wang Jian again compiled a book catalogue, totaling 5,074 scrolls.
25
南齊王亮、謝朏《四部書目》，凡一萬八千一十卷。 齊末兵火延燒秘閣，書籍煨燼。 梁元帝克平侯景，收公私經籍歸於江陵，凡七萬餘卷。 蓋佛老之書，計於其間。 及周師入郢，鹹自焚煬。 周武保定之中，官書裁盈萬卷。 平齊所得，數止五千。 及隋氏平陳，南北一統，秘書監牛弘奏請搜訪遺逸，著定書目，凡三萬餘卷。 煬帝寫五十副本，分為三品。 國家平王世充，收其圖籍，溯河西上，多有沉沒，存者重復八萬卷。
The Bibliographic Catalogue in Four Sections by Wang Liang and Xie Tiao of Southern Qi totaled 18,010 scrolls. At the end of Qi, military fires spread to the Secret Library, and the books were reduced to embers. When Emperor Yuan of Liang defeated Hou Jing, he collected public and private classics and books at Jiangling, totaling more than 70,000 scrolls. Buddhist and Daoist books were reckoned among them. When the Northern Zhou armies entered Ying, all were burned to ashes. Under Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou in the Baoding period, the imperial collection scarcely amounted to ten thousand scrolls. The books taken when Qi was conquered came to only five thousand scrolls. After the Sui conquered Chen and reunified the realm, Secretariat Director Niu Hong petitioned to recover lost texts and compile an official catalog, which came to more than thirty thousand scrolls. Emperor Yang ordered fifty duplicate sets made and ranked them in three grades. When the dynasty defeated Wang Shichong, it seized his library; much was lost in transport up the western Yellow River, yet what remained still came to eighty thousand scrolls.
26
自武德已後，文士既有修纂，篇卷滋多。 開元時，甲乙丙丁四部書各為一庫，置知書官八人分掌之。 凡四部庫書，兩京各一本，共一十二萬五千九百六十卷。 皆以益州麻紙寫。 其集賢院御書，經庫皆鈿白牙軸，黃縹帶，紅牙籤，史書庫鈿青牙軸，縹帶，綠牙籤，子庫皆雕紫檀軸，紫帶，碧牙籤，集庫皆綠牙軸，硃帶，白牙籤，以分別之。
From the Wude era on, as scholars continued to compile and edit texts, the number of works kept growing. During the Kaiyuan reign, the four library divisions each had its own vault, with eight bibliographic officers assigned to oversee them. The four repositories held complete sets in both capitals, for a combined total of 125,960 scrolls. All were copied on hemp paper from Yizhou. In the Academy of Assembled Worthies, the Classics used white inlaid ivory rollers with yellow silk ties and red tags; Histories used green inlaid ivory rollers with pale silk ties and green tags; Masters used carved rosewood rollers with purple ties and blue-green tags; and Collections used green ivory rollers with vermilion ties and white tags, so each division could be told apart at a glance.
